target.population: Mexico analytical-use design: adults aged 25-79 with no reported prior doctor diagnosis of diabetes/high blood sugar, recorded 8-12-hour fast, positive fasting serum glucose below 126 mg/dL, available HbA1c and valid standing anthropometry with internally consistent measurement documentation (uniformly excluding explicit not-weighed or alternative-standing-route documentation that contradicts usable standing measurements, without asserting which field is correct) under the prespecified measurement restrictions; pregnancy/lactation excluded when documented by questionnaire routing for women aged 25-49; no verified medication or anemia exclusion. Exactly 250 fictional individuals per female=0/1 crossed with age bands 25-39, 40-54, 55-69, 70-79; equal-stratum analytical design, not a nationally representative population.

lifelines.population: Lifelines western-European unrelated adults selected for GWAS, oldest family members preferred; n=2921 eligible; excludes self-reported diabetes or FPG>=7.0 mmol/L, significant anemia, and missing HbA1c/erythrocytes/FPG. Table 2 row-specific n unknown; Table 3 complete-case n unresolved. Monte Carlo reconstruction: assumed rounded normal age on 18-95 and independent female probability 0.597; 6000 fictional rows, not source IPD.

pani.population: Pani NHANES 2001-2004 n=3270, adults age>=25, no self-reported diabetes, FPG<126 mg/dL, HbA1c available. Complex survey design and weights. FOS context is different and is not pooled. NHANES overlaps Liu1999-2008. Monte Carlo reconstruction: assumed age support 25-95, published unweighted age-band count proportions used as approximate mixture probabilities, truncated geometric age tail >=70, and independent female probability 0.5; unweighted calculations are not the complex survey estimator; 6000 fictional rows, not source IPD.

hba1c_rule.coefficient_rule: solve the two distinct projection equations under the common assumed residual covariance
hba1c_rule.residual_rule: positive square root of reference HbA1c variance minus common model explained variance

assumptions.description: The computational domain is integer age 18-95, female coded 0/1, positive BMI and HbA1c, and positive fasting glucose strictly below 126 mg/dL. Age support is an author-imposed finite approximation, not an inferred source inclusion criterion. All values describe already-selected eligible individuals; no records of excluded people are generated.

The target has the required 250 people in each age-band by sex cell. Ages are uniform integers within each prescribed band, independently of subsequent residuals. Equal allocation and within-band uniformity are analytical design choices, not Mexican population frequencies.

Reconstruct the admitted Lifelines eligible Western-European GWAS source with independent sex Bernoulli(0.597) and rounded normal age with mean 55.5 and SD 9.9, rejecting ages outside 18-95. Actual source age limits and age-sex dependence are unknown. The finite support is assumed, includes ages outside target bounds, and may omit older people; oldest-family-member selection is represented only through the published age moments. Reported n=2921 is not the Monte Carlo size.

Reconstruct Pani NHANES 2001-2004 adults age>=25 without reported diabetes and FPG<126. Approximate age-band probabilities by the published unweighted counts [1037,330,322,261,198,283,198,641]/3270, not survey population weights. Ages are uniform integers below 70. In the open-ended >=70 band assume age=70+geometric(p=0.15)-1, rejecting ages above 95; 95 is an explicit computational cap, not the published upper age. Sex is independent Bernoulli(0.5), an assumption without source calibration. No Pani FOS data are pooled.

BMI and glucose have a shared conditional bivariate normal residual law. Conditional means change by +0.04 kg/m^2 BMI and +0.12 mg/dL glucose per year and by +0.5 kg/m^2 BMI and -1.0 mg/dL glucose for female=1. These dependence coefficients are author assumptions, not published estimates. Reference means and total SDs are from Lifelines. Positive BMI and 0<glucose<126 are enforced by joint residual rejection conditional on age and sex; this slightly perturbs untruncated moments and projections.

Set BMI-glucose residual correlation after age and sex to 0.30, which is unidentified by the admitted evidence. Derive two simultaneous HbA1c coefficients from the two separate Jansen Table 2 age/sex-adjusted projections using the declared residual covariance matrix. This is a conditional Gaussian algebraic identification assumption, not concatenation of published coefficients or a causal identification result. Other correlations would yield different structural coefficients.

Use Pani NHANES adjusted age coefficient 0.010 percentage points/year as a shared conditional linear age term across all contexts. Set the direct conditional female term to zero as an unidentifiable working assumption; this does not infer Jansen sex coding or claim no biological sex association. Age-sex interactions and nonlinear conditional age effects are omitted. Pani older marginal means suggest that linearity may be inadequate.

Assume independent homoscedastic normal HbA1c residuals. Derive variance as published Lifelines HbA1c SD^2 minus model-implied explained variance in the untruncated reference population, using the stated covariance and age/sex assumptions. Positive HbA1c is enforced by residual rejection. The resulting residual variation is individual stochastic variation, not uncertainty in regression coefficients, mean estimates, or transport.

A context may differ in one HbA1c reference level while all conditional slopes and residual laws are shared. Lifelines uses its published HbA1c mean 5.6 at the published reference age 55.5 and female fraction 0.597. Pani uses its 50-54 age-band mean 5.40 at assumed mean age 52 and female fraction 0.5. The latter anchor interprets the published weighted stratum mean under assumed within-band covariates. No other Pani age-band mean is used to repair the curve.

Target covariate mechanisms, residual covariance, residual HbA1c variation and conditional slopes are transported without Mexican recalibration from the shared source rule. The target takes exactly the Pani reference HbA1c level (5.40 at age 52), because a nondiabetic multi-ancestry US source is the chosen level anchor; geographical/ancestry similarity is not established. Lifelines supplies otherwise missing covariate dispersion. This hybrid transport is a scenario, not an estimated Mexican distribution. No target values or target-only scientific repair are used.

Selection on no reported diagnosis, valid measurements and fasting glucose is treated as already conditioned in the source summaries. The target serum assay is assumed numerically comparable to source plasma at fixed units, with no learned conversion; actual serum/plasma, fasting-duration, assay, ancestry, GWAS selection, pregnancy/lactation, standing-route and missingness differences are unresolved. Lifelines excluded significant anemia whereas the target has no verified anemia exclusion. No measured medication exclusion or unknown older-woman pregnancy/lactation status is invented. Unmeasured anemia/erythrocyte and medication effects are absorbed into a transported residual law, an unverified simplification.

All source checks use unweighted 6000-row Monte Carlo statistics on an assumed source reconstruction. Pani complex survey weights/design and Table2 complete analysis detail are not reconstructed. Checks are approximate projection diagnostics, not original-estimator replication. Published Table1 SEs are retained as evidence uncertainty and never converted to individual SDs. Jansen Table2 printed interval levels remain unknown.

One fixed parameter scenario is committed. Published rounding, unspecified Jansen interval confidence levels, Pani survey SEs, residual covariance, age support, nonlinear effects, assay and population transport remain evidence/model uncertainty; no probability distribution for that uncertainty is identified. Controller seeds change individuals only. Source agreement cannot validate Mexican target analyses or causal effects.

All five scientific variables are generated from the active aggregate context using the controller-supplied seed. Fictional identifiers encode context, seed and row number only. Rejection sampling rather than boundary clipping enforces positivity/glucose eligibility. No empirical moments are imposed on a realized draw, no fitted sample coefficients are computed, and no external data are read by the generator.

active_context.derivation: Only this selector changes across controller-created child specifications.

contexts.derivation: Target population/schema/count are copied from task. Source descriptions preserve published selection. Lifelines age and sex use Table1. Pani age-band counts are original Table1 counts in normalized_quantities.json; their use as mixture weights, within-band shapes, sex probability and age-52 anchor are assumptions. Pani>=70 extends to95. Target uses the same Pani anchor without target-derived repair.

reference_moments.derivation: Published Table1 marginal means/SDs and rounded female complement; glucose uses fixed18.0 conversion. Use published percent HbA1c5.6/0.3, not alternate rounded IFCC representation. Treat as nominal untruncated population moments for variance algebra, subject to small sampling/truncation differences.

covariate_dependence.derivation: Age/sex effects and residual correlation0.30 are explicit scientifically unidentified choices. They are neither extracted coefficients nor consequences of absent evidence.

hba1c_rule.derivation: For conditional residual variances vB,vG and covariance c, betaB=(pB-pG*c/vB)/(1-c*c/(vB*vG)), betaG=(pG-pB*c/vG)/(1-c*c/(vB*vG)). These satisfy two separate age/sex-adjusted projections in the assumed untruncated joint distribution. Add the separately transported Pani conditional age coefficient and assumed zero direct sex coefficient; determine independent HbA1c residual variance by reference variance decomposition.

simulation.derivation: A technical cap prevents unbounded rejection loops; it is not a biological parameter or a data-dependent tuning rule.
